sentence: This project measures the damage to nerve fibers and sensory cells in the inner ears of patients with common forms of acquired hearing loss.
This project tests whether chromatin modifying compounds can push neuroblastoma cells into a different state so that immunotherapy and small molecule inhibitors work better.
This project builds a single gene therapy that helps turn fibroblasts into beating heart cells to repair the heart after injury.
This project tries to find out which cellular and molecular changes cause mechanical itch and how acute itch turns into chronic itch.
This project runs a network of clinical trials in cancer that aims to find effective ways to prevent and treat cancer.
This project studies how genes are controlled in human metabolic tissues to understand what causes two types of fatty liver disease.
This project studies how gene mutations linked to autism change the activity of microglia, using stem cell derived microglia grown with cortical spheroids.
This project studies how pancreatic cancer changes its tumor microenvironment as it spreads, including the loss of its fibrous stroma.
This project studies how mice detect and respond to chemical signals from predators, and how this shapes their behavior.
This project isolates antibodies from allergic people to study how they bind mite, cat and dog allergens, and makes mutant allergens that are less allergenic.
This project tries to find out how radiation affects brain tumors in children and builds combined radioimmunotherapy treatments for them.
This project builds lipid nanoparticles that deliver gene silencing and gene editing molecules to tumors, and tests them in mouse models of cancer.
This project studies how the receptor VEGFR1 shapes the growth of blood vessels in the allantois and placenta.
This project builds paper-based tests and a DNA hydrogel platform that detect pathogen infection and can release a drug when the pathogen is found.
This project builds research software that helps scientists study how environmental and extreme weather exposures affect health.
This project tries to find out which molecular factors and pathways keep corneal epithelial cells growing and working normally.
This project studies how filovirus envelope glycoproteins work to help Ebola virus enter cells.
This project studies the physical properties of calcium-permeable glutamate receptors and how they shape brain development and plasticity.
This project studies how a modulator therapy changes lung and pancreas function in young children with cystic fibrosis.
This project studies how DNA modifications change in the brain during development and aging, and how these changes go wrong in human diseases.
